newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical found negligent in Louisiana trial.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical found negligent in Louisiana trial.

text.p: A state jury in a class-action lawsuit on Monday found Dow Chemical Co. was negligent in testing silicone for use in human implants and conspired with Dow Corning Inc.

The jury deliberated less than two days following five months of jury selection, trial testimony and courtroom skirmishes as Dow Chemical attorneys tried to have the trial stopped or transferred to Michigan.

The case, which now covers only the eight "class representatives" among 1,800 Louisiana women who recieved the Dow Corning implants, will move to phase two to determine if women have been injured as a result of the implants.

"This shows an American jury can't be fooled," the lead counsel for the women, John O'Quinn, said after the verdict was read. "Three out of three times, juries have evaluated all the evidence and found the giant chemical company guilty."

Juries awarded damages to individual plaintiffs in Nevada and Texas, he said. Thousands of women who recieved breast implants, 80 percent of which were for cosmetic purposes, claim to have suffered autoimmune and connective disorders as a result of the silicone implants.
